steps: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble is inversely proportional to its radius of curvature, given by P - P_0 = 4T/R.
For the hemispherical bubble at End 1, the radius of curvature is equal to the tube's radius, R_1 = r.
For the sub-hemispherical bubble at End 2, the radius of curvature R_2 is greater than the tube's radius r (R_2 > r).
Since R_1 < R_2, the pressure inside the bubble at End 1 is greater than the pressure at End 2 (P_1 > P_2).
Air flows from the region of higher pressure (End 1) to the region of lower pressure (End 2).
As air flows out of End 1, the volume of the soap bubble at End 1 decreases.
